tiles.label: Missed cases / yr: all-Canon vs all-Nikon

tiles.label: Equity gap at Nikon sites
tiles.sub: risk that a diseased patient is missed at a Nikon vs a Canon site: 24% vs 22% (sensitivity 0.84 vs 0.82 at spec 0.90; 18.60% vs 8.79% inadequate images)

tiles.label: What drives the gap?
tiles.sub: share of variance in the internal−external gap across 220 configurations; classifier 1%, resolution 0%

figures.title: Which tasks survive the camera change?
figures.caption: The paper's own internal (Canon) and external (Nikon) estimates with 95% bootstrap CIs. Orange = external drops ≥ 0.05; blue = external is higher (different case mix). ▶ = your task.

figures.title: Does a different classifier or resolution fix it?
figures.caption: Internal − external AUROC for all 220 binary configurations in Table 4. Rows (tasks) differ far more than columns (classifier × resolution).

figures.title: Your screening program: coverage vs camera quality
figures.caption: Missed referable cases per year (unscreened + ungradable + false negatives). Canon sites use the internal AUROC, Nikon sites the external one. A modelling illustration built on the paper's numbers.

figures.title: Why some tasks break: a synthetic mechanism
figures.caption: Simulated embeddings (not RETFound-Green). The Nikon 'camera' remixes colour/optical features. Tasks whose signal lives there degrade; cleaner (higher-resolution) features lift both lines but keep the gap.
